statements.claim: As the cowherds of Vraja slept in Ambika forest keeping a vow, the chief Nanda was seized by a great hungry serpent and cried out 'Krishna! Krishna!'
statements.evidence: SB 10.34.4-6: 'kaścin mahān ahis tasmin vipine 'ti-bubhukṣitaḥ' (a certain great serpent, very hungry, in that forest), 'sa cukrośāhinā grastaḥ kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahān ayam'; v18 confirms the cowherds completed their vow there ('samāpya tasmin niyamaṃ').

statements.claim: The cowherds beat and burned the serpent with firebrands, but it would not release Nanda.
statements.evidence: SB 10.34.7: 'alātair dahyamāno 'pi nāmuñcat tam uraṅgamaḥ' (though burnt by firebrands the serpent did not release him).

statements.claim: Krishna touched the serpent with his foot, which destroyed its evil and released Nanda.
statements.evidence: SB 10.34.8: 'sa vai bhagavataḥ śrīmat pāda-sparśa-hatāśubhaḥ' (its evil destroyed by the Lord's foot-touch); pack excerpt: 'Nanda was released'.

statements.claim: The serpent was in truth Sudarshana the Vidyadhara, who had mocked the Angirasa sages in pride of his beauty and been cursed by them as a grace — bound in the serpent body until the blessed one's touch should free him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.34.12-13: 'ṛṣīn virūpāṅgirasaḥ prāhasaṃ rūpa-darpitaḥ / śāpo me 'nugrahāyaiva kṛtas taiḥ karuṇātmabhiḥ'; identity as 'Sudarshana the Vidyadhara' comes from the pack's own source excerpt (SB 10.34.4-17 rendering), which the verses shown presuppose.

statements.claim: Krishna asked who he was, and the radiant being praised Krishna as the remover of fear for the refuge-seeking, the great yogi, then took leave, circumambulated him and bowed.
statements.evidence: SB 10.34.9-10 ('ko bhavān parayā lakṣmyā rocate 'dbhuta-darśanaḥ'), v14-15 ('bhava-bhītānāṃ prapannānāṃ bhayāpaham... mahā-yogin mahā-puruṣa sat-pate'), v17 ('ity anujñāpya dāśārhaṃ parikramyābhivandya ca').

statements.claim: The being then rose into the night sky (a Vidyadhara, sky-farer).
statements.evidence: The pack verses end with the circumambulation and homage (10.34.17); his skyward departure is not stated in the excerpted verses but is consistent with Vidyadhara nature and uncontradicted.

statements.claim: The cowherds, astonished at Krishna's glory, completed their vow and returned to Vraja telling the story.
statements.evidence: SB 10.34.18: 'niśāmya kṛṣṇasya tad ātma-vaibhavaṃ... samāpya tasmin niyamaṃ punar vrajaṃ... kathayanta ādṛtāḥ'.

notes: Faithful verse-by-verse to SB 10.34.4-18. The name/status 'Sudarshana the Vidyadhara' is carried by the pack's excerpt; dialogue paraphrase matches v9-16.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama, brought by Akrura, entered Mathura on foot along the royal road and were regarded with pleasure by men and women, like two young elephants.
statements.evidence: VP 5.19 (pack): 'You must now journey on foot... left them... whilst Ráma and Krishńa continued to walk along the royal road. Regarded with pleasure by men and women, they went along sportively, looking like two young elephants.'

statements.claim: A weaver gladly fitted both brothers with garments of many colours, each bearing its own mark/device.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.39-40: 'vāyakaḥ prītas tayor veṣam akalpayat / nānā-lakṣaṇa-veṣābhyāṃ kṛṣṇa-rāmau virejatuḥ'.

statements.claim: Pleased with the weaver, Krishna gave him a form like his own (sārūpya).
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.41: 'tasya prasanno bhagavān prādāt sārūpyam ātmanaḥ'.

statements.claim: At the garland-maker Sudama's house the brothers were honoured with seats, foot-washing water, arghya and other rites, and with garlands and sandal paste.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.42-43 ('sudāmno bhavanaṃ mālā-kārasya... āsanam ānīya pādyaṃ cārghyārhaṇādibhiḥ') and pack excerpt ('honoring them with garlands and sandal paste').

statements.claim: Sudama declared their birth and family purified, called them the supreme cause of the world with no partial glance, the soul of all beings, and offered himself as their servant.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.44-47: 'naḥ sārthakaṃ janma pāvitaṃ ca kulaṃ... viśvasya jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ param... na hi vāṃ viṣamā dṛṣṭiḥ suhṛdor jagad-ātmanoḥ / tāv ajñāpayataṃ bhṛtyaṃ kim ahaṃ karavāṇi vām'.

statements.claim: Asked what he wanted, Sudama chose only unshakable devotion, and Krishna granted it along with fortune that grows in his line.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.50-51: 'so 'pi vavre 'calāṃ bhaktiṃ tasminn evākhilātmani / iti tasmai varaṃ dattvā śriyaṃ cānvaya-vardhinīm'.

statements.claim: The older telling adds that the blessing extended beyond this life to a heavenly region at the end.
statements.evidence: VP 5.19 (pack excerpt): 'you shall finally obtain... a heavenly region, the consequence of my favour'; tradition_note correctly flags this as the VP-only framing.

statements.claim: Word of the strangers spread through Mathura that night; the city wondered what the cowherd boys would do next.
statements.evidence: Closing scene-setting consistent with the canonical sequence (the brothers are in Kamsa's city before the arena events); not a sourceable assertion in the pack.

notes: Blends BP 10.41.39-51 (weaver + Sudama, sārūpya and devotion/fortune boons) with VP 5.19 (foot-entry, heavenly region), cleanly attributed; tradition_note matches the pack's variant note.

statements.claim: The radiant being before Krishna had been a giant lizard in a dry well, drawn out by Krishna's left hand and restored by his touch — King Nriga of the Ikshvaku line.
statements.evidence: Recap of the canonical prior event (corpus chain, previous title): 'The Yadu princes find a giant lizard in a well; Krishna pulls it out with his left hand, and it becomes the radiant King Nriga'; Nriga's Ikshvaku lineage per pack index.

statements.claim: Nriga gave cows beyond counting — as many as the sands of the earth and stars of the sky: milch and young cows of fine form, tawny with gold-tipped horns, to virtuous, vow-keeping brahmanas and needy families.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.11-13: 'yāvatyaḥ sikatā bhūmer yāvatyo divi tārakāḥ / payasvinīs taruṇīḥ śīla-rūpa-guṇopapannāḥ kapilā hema-sṛṅgīḥ / sv-alaṅkṛtebhyo guṇa-śīlavadbhyaḥ sīdat-kuṭumbebhya ṛta-vratebhyaḥ'.

statements.claim: He also gave land, gold, houses, horses, elephants, maidens with their servants, sesame, silver and beds.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.14: 'go-bhū-hiraṇyāyatanāśva-hastinaḥ kanyāḥ sa-dāsīs tila-rūpya-śayyāḥ'.

statements.claim: A cow of a foremost brahmana strayed into Nriga's herd and was being led out to another brahmana when its owner cried 'That cow is mine!'; both brahmanas disputed the cow before the king.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.15-17: 'kasyacid dvija-mukhyasya bhraṣṭā gaur mama go-dhane / tāṃ nīyamānāṃ tat-svāmī dṛṣṭvovāca mameti tam / viprau vivadamānau mām ūcatuḥ svārtha-sādhakau'.

statements.claim: Nriga propitiated both brahmanas with wealth gained by righteous means, begging them to forgive the unknowing servant; the owner refused all compensation and walked away, and neither would yield.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.18-20: 'anunītāv ubhau viprau dharma-kṛcchra-gatena vai / bhavantāv anugṛhītāṃ kiṅkarasyāvijānataḥ / nāhaṃ pratīcche vai rājann ity uktvā svāmy apākramat'; pack summary: 'both brahmanas claimed it and refused all compensation'.

statements.claim: Yama's messengers took Nriga to Yama's court, where Yama asked whether he would first taste the good or the bad of his deeds.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.21-22: 'etasminn antare yāmair dūtair nīto yama-kṣayam / pūrvaṃ tvam aśubhaṃ bhuṅkṣa utāho nṛpate śubham'.

statements.claim: Nriga chose to suffer the bad first, and so fell as a lizard.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.23: 'pūrvaṃ devāśubhaṃ bhuñja iti prāha pateti saḥ'; pack excerpt: 'he fell as a lizard'. The dry-well imprisonment is the established prior-event state (corpus chain).

statements.claim: The moralizing gloss on Nriga's motives ('perhaps because the merit of a life of giving could wait...') is offered as the narrator's speculation.
statements.evidence: Explicitly framed as conjecture ('He did not argue it. Perhaps...'); no factual claim.

notes: Follows SB 10.64.9-23 closely; well/left-hand/lizard details belong to the preceding canonical event and are consistent with the pack chain.

statements.claim: Nriga praised Krishna as the witness of every being's heart, the lord of yoga seen in the pure hearts of those guided by scripture, beyond the senses, whose very sight ends worldly existence.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.24-25: 'kiṃ nu te 'viditaṃ nātha sarva-bhūtātma-sākṣiṇaḥ... parātmā yogeśvaraḥ śruti-dṛśāmala-hṛd-vibhāvyaḥ sākṣād adhokṣaja... yasya bhavāpavargaḥ'.

statements.claim: Nriga asked Krishna's permission to go to the celestial world, bowed, circumambulated him and touched his feet with his head.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.26-29: 'anujānīhi māṃ kṛṣṇa yāntaṃ deva-gatiṃ prabho... ity uktvā taṃ parikramya pādau spṛṣṭvā sva-maulinā'.

statements.claim: Krishna taught the gathered citizens that a brahmana's property, even a little enjoyed, is indigestible fire — worse than hālāhala poison (which has an antidote; poison kills only the eater and fire is quenched by water), for brahmana wealth taken without leave destroys three generations.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.31-34: 'durjaraṃ bata brahma-svaṃ bhuktam agner manāg api / nāhaṃ hālāhalaṃ manye viṣaṃ yasya pratikriyā / hinasti viṣam attāraṃ vahnir adbhiḥ praśāmyati / brahma-svaṃ duranujñātaṃ bhuktaṃ hanti tri-pūruṣam'.

statements.claim: Krishna warned that kings blinded by royal fortune do not see their own fall, paying in years for every handful of dust and every tear of those they rob.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.35-37: 'rājāno rāja-lakṣmyāndhā nātma-pātaṃ vicakṣate / gṛhṇanti yāvataḥ pāṃśūn krandatām aśru-bindavaḥ / rājāno rāja-kulyāś ca tāvato 'bdān niraṅkuśāḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna declared that whoever takes a brahmana's livelihood — given by his own hand or another's — covets what makes men short-lived; that one must never harm even an erring brahmana; and that wealth torn from a brahmana drags the taker down.
statements.evidence: SB 10.64.38-42: 'sva-dattāṃ para-dattāṃ vā brahma-vṛttiṃ harec ca yaḥ / na me brahma-dhanaṃ bhūyād yad gṛdhvālpāyuṣo narāḥ / vipraṃ kṛtāgasam api naiva druhyata māmakāḥ / yathāhaṃ praṇame viprān anukālaṃ samāhitaḥ / brāhmaṇārtho hy apahṛto hartāraṃ pātayaty adhaḥ'.

statements.claim: A celestial car descended, Nriga boarded it and ascended out of sight above Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Nriga praised Krishna, bowed, and ascended to heaven in a celestial car'; consistent with SB 10.64's continuation beyond the excerpted v43 ('evaṃ viśrāvya bhagavān mukundo dvārakaukasaḥ').

statements.claim: The two teachings — the poison-with-no-antidote warning and Nriga's tale — were retold in Dwaraka long after.
statements.evidence: Closing reflection; not a sourceable assertion.

notes: Teaching matches SB 10.64.30-43 near-verbatim. Note: the pack's one-line excerpt condenses the order (ascent before the teaching); the passage itself (and this story) place Krishna's address to the people first, the car/ascent after — passage treated as authoritative.

statements.claim: Paundraka, king of Karusha, deluded by flatterers who called him the descended Lord Vasudeva, lost recollection of his real self and believed himself the one true Vasudeva.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.1-2 ('tvaṃ vāsudevo bhagavān avatīrṇo jagat-patiḥ', 'dūtaṃ ca prāhiṇon mandaḥ'); VP 5.34: 'flattered by ignorant people as the descended deity... Losing all recollection of his real character'.

statements.claim: He sent a messenger to Krishna at Dwaraka demanding that Krishna give up the divine marks he bore and surrender the name and character of Vasudeva, coming to do homage in return for means of subsistence.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.4-5 ('vāsudevo 'vatīrṇo 'ham eka eva na cāparaḥ / yāni tvam asmac-cihnāni mauḍhyād bibharṣi sātvata'); VP 5.34 message: 'Relinquish... the discus; lay aside all my insignia, my name, and the character of Vāsudeva; and come and do me homage; and I will vouchsafe thee means of subsistence.'

statements.claim: The assembly laughed at the message, and Krishna replied in jesting words that he would hurl those very signs at the fool and slay him, and that Paundraka's face would lie covered by cranes and vultures.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.7-9: 'uvāca dūtaṃ bhagavān parihāsa-kathām anu / mukhaṃ tad apidhāyājña kaṅka-gṛdhra-vaṭair vṛtaḥ'; pack excerpt: 'the assembly laughed, and Krishna replied that he would hurl those signs at the fool and slay him'; VP 5.34: the assembly/jesting reply and ironic discus promise.

statements.claim: The messenger carried the whole reply back to Paundraka, unsoftened.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.10 (pack v9): 'iti dūtas tam ākṣepaṃ svāmine sarvam āharat'.

statements.claim: Paundraka had made ready for a penitent Krishna — the welcome, the ceremonies.
statements.evidence: Nothing in the pack (SB 10.66.1-9 and excerpt) or in the fuller account (SB 10.66.10-11 shows Paundraka instead appearing with two akṣauhiṇīs to meet Krishna's battle preparations; VP 5.34 likewise has him march out with his army) supports any prepared welcome or ceremonies for a submitting Krishna.

statements.claim: The story's closing note that his delusion left no room for the possibility that his embassy was absurd.
statements.evidence: Dramatization consistent with the delusion the pack establishes; not itself a sourceable event.

corrections.original_sentence: He had made ready for a penitent Krishna — the welcome, the ceremonies — and the thought that the demand might be refused had never once crossed his mind.
corrections.suggested: He had been certain of his own divinity, and the thought that the demand might be refused had never once crossed his mind.

notes: Core episode faithful to SB 10.66.1-9. One invented embellishment: the welcome/ceremonies prepared for a 'penitent Krishna' — no source has Paundraka preparing ceremonies; both SB and VP show him arming for battle instead.

statements.claim: Krishna had slain the impostor Paundraka and the king of Kashi who had sheltered him; the king's son Sudakshina performed his father's funeral rites.
statements.evidence: Prior canonical event (corpus chain: 'Krishna Slays Paundraka and the King of Kashi'); VP 5.34: Paundraka 'supported by the king of Káśí. Krishńa marches against, and destroys them.'; SB 10.66.25-26: 'rājñaḥ kāśī-pater... mahiṣyaḥ putra-bāndhavāḥ / sudakṣiṇas tasya sutaḥ kṛtvā saṃsthā-vidhiṃ pateḥ'.

statements.claim: With his teachers Sudakshina worshipped Shiva at Avimukta, and the pleased lord granted him a boon: to serve the southern (dakṣiṇa) fire with brahmana priests in an abhicāra rite against the enemy he called impious.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.27-30: 'ity ātmanābhisandhāya sopādhyāyo maheśvaram / prīto 'vimukte bhagavāṃs tasmai varam adād vibhuḥ / dakṣiṇāgniṃ paricara brāhmaṇaiḥ samam ṛtvijam / sādhayiṣyati saṅkalpam abrahmaṇye prayojitaḥ'.

statements.claim: From the fire pit rose an embodied, terrible fire-demon — fierce with fangs, furrowed brows and a harsh face, tongue licking, feet of palm-tree size shaking the earth — which set out toward Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.31-34: 'tato 'gnir utthitaḥ kuṇḍān mūrtimān ati-bhīṣaṇaḥ / daṃṣṭrogra-bhru-kuṭī-daṇḍa-kaṭhorāsyaḥ sva-jihvayā / padbhyāṃ tāla-pramāṇābhyāṃ kampayann avanī-talam / tam ābhicāra-dahanam āyāntaṃ dvārakaukasaḥ'.

statements.claim: The frightened citizens of Dwaraka ran to Krishna, who was playing dice in the assembly hall; Krishna, witness within and without all things, saw the fear of his people and sent the Sudarshana discus, blazing like ten million suns and like the fire of cosmic dissolution.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.35-38: 'akṣaiḥ sabhāyāṃ krīḍantaṃ bhagavantaṃ bhayāturāḥ... sarvasyāntar-bahiḥ-sākṣī vibhuḥ / tat sūrya-koṭi-pratimaṃ sudarśanaṃ jājvalyamānaṃ pralayānala-prabham'.

statements.claim: The demon, its face shattered by the discus, turned back and, reaching Varanasi, burned Sudakshina and the priests — his own abhicāra consumed its master.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.39: 'kṛtyānalaḥ pratihataḥ... bhagna-mukho nivṛttaḥ / vārāṇasīṃ parisametya sudakṣiṇaṃ taṃ sartvig-janaṃ samadahat sva-kṛto 'bhicāraḥ'.

statements.claim: The discus then entered Varanasi — through its ramparts, halls and markets — and burned the whole city, which even the gods could not enter, with all its princes and followers.
statements.evidence: SB 10.66.40-42: 'cakraṃ ca viṣṇos tad-anupraviṣṭaṃ vārāṇasīṃ sāṭṭa-sabhālayāpaṇām / dagdhvā vārāṇasīṃ sarvāṃ'; VP 5.34: 'Thus was Vārāṇasī burnt, with all its princes and their followers... a city, that was inaccessible to the gods, was thus wrapped in flames.'

statements.claim: The closing moral — that the discus undid in a single night what no army or god had ever done to the city he loved — is rhetorical summation.
statements.evidence: The 'single night' duration is not stated in the pack; the sentence is a moralizing close (compare VP's 'inaccessible to the gods'), not an event report.

notes: Faithful to SB 10.66.25-42 and VP 5.34; Sudakshina's name follows BP while the pack's variant note flags VP leaves the son unnamed.

statements.claim: At the svayamvara of Lakshmana, daughter of Duryodhana, Samba — son of Jambavati and a Yadava of Dwaraka — carried her off in his chariot.
statements.evidence: VP 5.35 (pack): 'At the choice of a husband by the daughter of Duryodhana, the princess was carried off by the hero Śámba, the son of Jámbavatí'; BP 10.68.1ff, Kauravas' outcry follows (v1-2, 5).

statements.claim: The furious Kauravas called him an ill-mannered boy, demanded he be bound, and asked what the Vrishnis would dare do.
statements.evidence: SB 10.68.1-3: 'kauravāḥ kupitā ūcur durvinīto 'yam arbhakaḥ / badhnītemaṃ durvinītaṃ kiṃ kariṣyanti vṛṣṇayaḥ'.

statements.claim: Karna, Shala, Bhuri, Yajnaketu and Duryodhana himself gave chase, shouting 'Stop! Stop!'
statements.evidence: SB 10.68.4-6: 'iti karṇaḥ śalo bhūrir yajñaketuḥ suyodhanaḥ / dṛṣṭvānudhāvataḥ sāmbo dhārtarāṣṭrān mahā-rathaḥ / taṃ te jighṛkṣavaḥ kruddhās tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti bhāṣiṇaḥ'; story follows BP's five chiefs (tradition_note correct that VP adds Bhishma and Drona).

statements.claim: Samba turned, twanged his handsome bow and pierced them all — four arrows into the horses of each foremost chariot and one arrow into each charioteer.
statements.evidence: SB 10.68.8-9: 'visphūrjya ruciraṃ cāpaṃ sarvān vivyādha sāyakaiḥ / caturbhiś caturo vāhān ekaikena ca sārathīn'.

statements.claim: The Kurus cut down his four horses and, with great effort, seized and bound him, chariot-less, taking him prisoner with Lakshmana taken from him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.68.10-11: 'taṃ tu te virathaṃ cakruś catvāraś caturo hayān / taṃ baddhvā virathī-kṛtya kṛcchreṇa kuravo yudhi'; the recovery of Lakshmana into Kuru hands is implied by the failed abduction at Hastinapura (uncontradicted in the pack; VP 5.35 later has the Kurus surrender 'Śámba and his wife').

statements.claim: The attitude among Kauravas that the Yadu race had no claim to royal dignity.
statements.evidence: VP 5.35 (pack): 'Báhlíka and other friends of the Kauravas, who looked upon the Yadu race as not entitled to regal dignity'; echoed in BP's 'kiṃ kariṣyanti vṛṣṇayaḥ'.

statements.claim: When the Yadavas heard of the capture, their wrath was kindled and Dwaraka's councils grew hot with talk of war.
statements.evidence: SB 10.68.12: 'tac chrutvā nāradoktena rājan sañjāta-manyavaḥ'; VP 5.35: 'their wrath was kindled against Duryodhana and his associates, and they prepared to take up arms against them'.

notes: Faithful to SB 10.68.1-12 following the BP chief-list; VP variant (Bhishma/Drona among pursuers) correctly noted in tradition_note.

statements.claim: Narada, astonished that Krishna with a single body had married so many women, came to Dwaraka to see it for himself.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.1-2: 'citraṃ bataitad ekena vapuṣā yugapat pṛthak... ity utsuko dvāravatīṃ devarṣir draṣṭum āgamat'.

statements.claim: Dwaraka was adorned with nine hundred thousand palaces of crystal and silver, with well-laid roads, squares and marketplaces.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.4-5: 'prāsāda-lakṣair navabhir juṣṭāṃ sphāṭika-rājataiḥ / vibhakta-rathyā-patha-catvarāpaṇaiḥ śālā-sabhābhī rucirāṃ surālayaiḥ'.

statements.claim: The inner quarter held sixteen thousand mansions of coral pillars and beryl floors, canopies hung with pearls, jewel lamps dispelling darkness, peacocks on the roofs, and maidservants in gold necklaces and fine robes.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.7-11: 'ṣoḍaśabhiḥ sadma-sahasraiḥ... viṣṭabdhaṃ vidruma-stambhair vaidūrya-phalakottamaiḥ / vitānair... muktā-dāma-vilambibhiḥ / dāsībhir niṣka-kaṇṭhībhiḥ su-vāsobhir alaṅkṛtam / ratna-pradīpa-nikara-dyutibhir nirasta-dhvāntaṃ vicitra-valabhīṣu śikhaṇḍino'.

statements.claim: In the first mansion Narada saw Krishna on a couch fanned by Rukmini; the Lord rose, bowed, seated the sage, washed his feet and took that water on his own head, then asked what he might do for him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.12-15: wife fanning him with a gold-handled chowrie; 'sahasotthita... ānamya pāda-yugalaṃ śirasā... sāñjalir avīviśad āsane sve / tasyāvanijya caraṇau tad-apaḥ sva-mūrdhnā bibhraj... prāha prabho bhagavate karavāma he kim'. The first queen is identified as Rukmini in the standard expanded telling (Krishna Book, ch. 69) and the pack lists Rukmini among the event's characters.

statements.claim: Narada praised Krishna — friendship to all beings, restraint toward the wicked, a free descent for the world's good — and asked that he might always remember the Lord's feet, the refuge of those fallen in the well of the world.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.16-17: 'maitrī janeṣu sakaleṣu damaḥ khalānām... svairāvatāra urugāya... dṛṣṭaṃ tavāṅghri-yugalaṃ janatāpavargaṃ... saṃsāra-kūpa-patitottaraṇāvalambaṃ dhyāyaṃś carāmy anugṛhāṇa yathā smṛtiḥ syāt'.

statements.claim: Palace by palace Narada saw Krishna at once playing dice with a wife and Uddhava (asked 'when did you arrive?' as if unaware), cuddling small children, pouring oblations in the five great sacrifices, at twilight japa, riding horses/elephants/chariots, counselling ministers including Uddhava, giving adorned cows to brahmanas, laughing at a jest with his beloved, meditating alone on the Person beyond nature, warring and making peace, performing weddings and thread ceremonies of his children, worshipping the gods, and hunting on a Sindhu horse.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.18-34: 'dīvyantam akṣais tatrāpi priyayā coddhavena ca / pṛṣṭaś cāviduṣevāsau kadāyāto bhavān iti / lālayantaṃ sutān śiśūn / juhvantaṃ ca vitānāgnīn yajantaṃ pañcabhir makhaiḥ / sandhyām upāsīnaṃ japantaṃ brahma vāg-yatam / aśvair gajai rathaiḥ... vicarantaṃ / mantrayantaṃ... mantribhiś coddhavādibhiḥ / dadataṃ gāḥ sv-alaṅkṛtāḥ / hasantaṃ hāsa-kathayā... priyayā / dhyāyantam ekam āsīnaṃ puruṣaṃ prakṛteḥ param / kurvantaṃ vigrahaṃ kaiścit sandhiṃ cānyatra / prasthāpanopanayanair apatyānāṃ mahotsavān / yajantaṃ sakalān devān... / carantaṃ mṛgayāṃ... hayam āruhya saindhavam'.

statements.claim: In every mansion Krishna was wholly present, and in none was he diminished; each greeted the sage with complete attention.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.35 ('avyakta-lingaṃ prakṛtiṣv antaḥ-pura-gṛhādiṣu') and the repeated greeting motif of v20-22; pack excerpt: 'saw Krishna everywhere at once... in each of the 16,000 mansions'.

statements.claim: Narada laughed, said he knew Krishna's yoga-maya, which even clever illusionists cannot see, and asked leave to wander the worlds flooded with Krishna's glory.
statements.evidence: SB 10.69.36-38: 'nāradaḥ prahasann iva / vidāma yoga-māyās te durdarśā api māyinām / anujānīhi māṃ deva lokāṃs te yaśasāplutān'; Krishna's assent and bidding him wander is the following canonical event (corpus chain next title).

notes: Closely follows SB 10.69.1-38; each household activity maps to its verse. Rukmini's identification in the first palace is standard in the tradition (Krishna Book) and consistent with the pack's character list.
